settings.heading: The mixed-revenue kitchen
settings.text: At Savi, rooms only held after corporate MICE banquets ran morning to evening and walk-in family lunches shared the same kitchen and service spine. Mixed revenue, not a single hero dish.

settings.heading: Menu before merch
settings.text: At Siya, every historical menu was digitised before repricing. Culinary families, seasonals, rotational pop-ups, print-ready composition. The storefront inherits that order: rooms that exist before merchandise shouts.

settings.heading: Kill gates
settings.text: The leased-hotel hold was returned when the thesis failed — offboarding records, inventory state, a pitchbook. The house keeps that honesty: stop when the work will not hold.

settings.heading: Software as mise en place
settings.text: Kartavya also builds software — restaurant platforms, hospitality automation, this storefront. Code is prep: labelled, rotated, ready for service. It is not the tasting menu.

settings.heading: Four rooms, still in draft
settings.text: Forge for skillets, Terre for clay, Kuro for knives, Sets for hybrid service. Collection doors are framed before products publish — empty rooms on purpose, not stock filler.

settings.heading: Opening the door
settings.text: About, Story, Building of, Journal. Add entries as the kitchen advances. Keep the voice of the house — synthesis as ambition, evidence tags where claims appear, no invented performance numbers.

settings.heading: Building of
settings.lede: A making-of journal for the house: how hotel F&B and restaurant menus became a product house, and how the storefront is composed. Living notes, sourced from published work — not a fab sheet.
